Pile of American Buffalo skulls to be used for fertilizer. c. 1875

American Buffalo (aka bison) hunting was an activity fundamental to the Midwestern Native Americans, which was later adopted by American professional hunters, They were hunted for their skins, with the rest of the animal left behind to decay on the ground. Hides were prepared and shipped to the east and Europe for processing into leather. Homesteaders collected bones from carcasses left by hunters to be used in refining sugar and making fertilizer and fine bone china. Bison bones brought from $2.50 to $15.00 a ton. There are perhaps 180,000 skulls on this pile.

The large scale hunting led to the near-extinction of the species. It is estimated that there were 60 million bison around 1800 and the population had shrunk to about 300 by 1900. By 2000 the population had recovered to about 360,000.

Would take some time to find but I have statements to prove you wrong.

In my experience in working with payment processors this is usually how long they like to take. Can they process transactions instantly? Yes. Do they? No. Can a retailer wait for your original payment to process before posting refunds? Yes.

Most large retailers have enough cash in bank to have a lot of floating transactions but you don't always want to float transactions because of fraud and charge backs. In the case of returns, it is in the retailers best interest to let the original transaction process before returning the funds, hence the 3-5 day turn around.

If you use a card at a brick-and-mortar store, you receive a full refund if the original transaction occurred the same day, AND the value of you purchase and refund are the same.

Otherwise your refund usually takes 3 to 5 business days. This can vary from one location to another based on how they process their credit transactions. Furthermore, the end-of-month billing and credit process may delay all transactions.
